subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Anatomy of a Coffee Cherry
description: One-minute skill: Anatomy of a Coffee Cherry.

hook.text: A coffee bean isn't a bean at all. It's the seed inside a fruit called a coffee cherry.

buildup.text: Each cherry has skin, pulp, parchment, silver skin, and finally two seeds nestled face-to-face.

discovery.text: The mucilage layer—a sweet, sticky coating around the seed—plays a huge role in flavor during processing.

twist.text: About 5% of cherries contain just one round seed instead of two. These are called peaberries.

climax.text: Every layer of the cherry contributes to the final cup. Remove pulp differently and the flavor changes.

punchline.text: Your coffee started as a fruit. The seed is the star.

quiz.question: What is a peaberry?
options: A cherry with one round seed instead of two

details.summary: A coffee cherry has layers: outer skin, mucilage, parchment, silverskin, and the seed we call a bean. Each layer affects flavor during processing. Most cherries contain two beans, but peaberries have just one, which some believe produces a sweeter, more concentrated cup.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding cherry anatomy explains why processing methods like washed, natural, and honey produce such different flavors from the same plant.
takeaways: Coffee beans are seeds inside a fruit called a cherry
Each cherry layer influences the final flavor profile
Peaberries are single-seed cherries prized for intensity

faq.question: What is the difference between a coffee cherry and a coffee bean?
faq.answer: The cherry is the whole fruit that grows on the coffee plant. The bean is the seed inside. What we roast and brew is the seed after the fruit layers have been removed through wet or dry processing methods.

faq.question: Why are peaberries considered special?
faq.answer: Peaberries form when only one seed develops inside the cherry instead of two. This single bean absorbs all the nutrients, potentially creating a more concentrated flavor. They are hand-sorted and often sold at a premium.
